Robot writes down what it hears, on this phone, line by line, and saves each line as it goes. It keeps working with the screen off; the notification is on the whole time, with Pause and Stop. “FR?” means the line was too short to tell its language: tap it to fix. With speaker labels on (Settings › Conversation), each line says who spoke: S1, S2… or the name you give (tap the chip; long-press a line if someone else said it). Very short replies go to whoever spoke just before, two people talking at once go to one of them, and the same person near and far from the phone can become two speakers: merge them. Translate shows each line in the other language (fast first when the fast engine is installed, then Robot\'s model; tap a translation for a better one); Speak reads the translations aloud, and Robot doesn\'t listen while it speaks. The Interpreter (in the menu) is for two people face to face: the top half turns to them. Nothing said to Robot while its panel is open is transcribed, and “hey robot” sleeps during the session unless you turn on Settings › Conversation › “Hey robot works during a conversation”. The audio is never kept.

Start a transcript from Home, the Quick Settings tile “Transcribe”, a long press on Robot\'s icon, or say “hey robot, transcribe this conversation”. Transcripts are kept in Robot\'s private storage on this phone and never backed up. The audio is never kept.

Live words: the words of the line being spoken, in grey, while the transcript is on screen (uses more battery; off when the phone is warm). “Hey robot” during a conversation: on, it pauses the transcript and opens Robot, and what you say to Robot isn\'t transcribed; off, the wake word sleeps while Robot transcribes, so nobody\'s “hey robot” opens it, “stop” still works while Robot talks, and the wake word is back when you stop. Start from the lock screen: the tile and “hey robot” can start a transcript while the phone is locked; that screen shows only what it hears from then on, and reading, exporting and deleting transcripts need the phone unlocked.

Speakers: Robot can label who says what in a transcript, by their voices: S1, S2… or the names you give (tap a line\'s speaker). It all happens on this phone; the voices are forgotten when the transcript stops. The speaker model is a pinned file, checked (SHA-256) before Robot uses it. %1$s Past the most speakers, a new voice goes to the nearest speaker; the interpreter always tells two people apart. Your voice, optional: read three short sentences so your lines say “You” instead of S1 or S2. Robot keeps a voiceprint (numbers made from your voice, not the recording), encrypted on this phone, used only for this and never sent anywhere. A voiceprint is biometric data; delete it here any time.

Translate transcripts: each line in the other language (%1$s), under it, on this phone: at once by the fast engine when it is downloaded, then better by Robot\'s model. The transcript screen\'s Translate turns it on or off for one transcript. The interpreter always translates. Offer a stronger AI first: for a long conversation (about half an hour or more), one marked important, or a summary whose check found something missing, Robot offers a stronger AI first. Nothing is sent before you tap Send on its card.

Fast translation: Robot\'s fast translation engine translates French ↔ English on this phone in a fraction of a second, in a process of its own: Mozilla\'s Bergamot models, run by slimt. Once it is downloaded, each transcript line gets its translation at once (marked “fast”) and Robot\'s model then replaces it with a better one; in the interpreter it stands in when Robot\'s model is slow, and leads when the model runs on the CPU. Without it, Robot\'s model translates alone, more slowly. From Mozilla\'s servers, the files each direction needs: %1$s to download, %2$s in Robot\'s private storage. Each is checked (SHA-256) before Robot uses it. Wi-Fi recommended.

Test translation speed translates Robot\'s %1$d test lines (Québec French and English) and compares each with what the same engine gave on the build machine. The mark: a median of %2$d ms a line or less, %3$d MB or less with both directions loaded, and every line the same. Only the test\'s own sentences are translated. While this page shows, the engine stays loaded: `adb shell dumpsys meminfo %4$s:mt` shows its memory.
